clauses.reason: The order's only operative command, "I hereby approve said amendments and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended", approves a code of fair competition under section 3 of Title I of NIRA, and the approved code had legal effect only through section 3. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The repeal therefore extinguished the prospective operative effect of the approval on June 14, 1935; the resolution states no later effective date, and no held record ends the approval earlier. The order approves amendments proposed by the Federal Alcohol Control Administration after notice and hearing and restates the approval of the code in its entirety as amended; it acts under Title I of NIRA, so the approval and the amendments both rest on the section 3 power.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 7018 of April 19, 1935 approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry and restates the approval of the code as amended, under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA); its only operative command is that approval. The text states no period, condition, 'until' date or provisional approval, and no held record cancels, suspends, supersedes or modifies the approval under section 10(b) before June 14, 1935. The approval had legal effect only through section 3 (standards of fair competition under 3(b), equity enforcement under 3(c), misdemeanor liability under 3(f)). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375), approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions delegating power to approve or prescribe codes and providing for their enforcement, so the best supported first end of the approval's prospective operative effect is June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end. Acts and liabilities before the repeal are accrued effects.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or modified under section 10(b) before June 14, 1935. I read the order's full text (signed April 19, 1935; no stated period, condition, 'until' date or provisional approval) and searched the held order texts for the code name and this order's number; the lookups report that it is the latest of several held orders amending the Distilled Spirits Industry code (Executive Orders 6756-D of June 29, 1934, 6811 of August 4, 1934 and 7000 of April 5, 1935 are the earlier ones) and no held order cancels or supersedes the code. The WPA list entry for this order (1935 Apr 19, p.610) records the approval only. The OFR catalog starts in 1937, so it cannot show 1933-1935 endings, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches name this order nowhere. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced the June 16, 1935 expiry of Title I with April 1, 1936. Signed April 19, 1935, the order precedes the June 14, 1935 repeal by eight weeks and states no own-terms end.","independent_command_check":"The order contains no appointment, delegation, direction to an agency, report requirement, committee or other command independent of the code approval; its single operative sentence approves the amendments and modifies the previous approval of the code.","savings_check":"Savings are the accrued effects described in the savings reason (S.J. Res. 113 and NIRA section 5 as held). The repeal's section 2 states no savings clause of its own; the held sources show no prosecution or enforcement continuing after June 14, 1935 and nothing that keeps the approval operative.","scope_check":"The inventory is the order's single clause (the whole short text). Its operative sentence is \"I hereby approve said amendments and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended\". The two Whereas paragraphs (the Federal Alcohol Control Administration's submission of the amendments, and notice and hearing) are recitals, not commands. The order acts under Title I of NIRA, so the approval of the amendments and the restated approval of the code both rest on the section 3 power, and section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 reaches all of it."}

savings.reason: Fines, injunctions, convictions, liabilities and acts done under this code before June 14, 1935 are completed effects that the repeal left in place; the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the code taken before the repeal is likewise accrued, subject to the resolution's proviso, whose effect on pre-repeal action under codes the held text does not settle. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, judgment: the code provisions in question were held invalid on the delegation ground and on the intrastate-commerce ground. Recorded as a validity characterization of section 3 code approvals, not as an end date; the delegation holding itself is in the opinion of the Court.
